formulas.title: Basic Arithmetic Formula
formulas.worked: =A1*B1 multiplies the value in A1 by the value in B1
formulas.note: Every Excel formula must begin with an equals sign so the program interprets it as a calculation, not text.

formulas.title: SUM Function Syntax
formulas.worked: =SUM(A1:A10) adds every value from cell A1 through A10
formulas.note: SUM ignores empty or text cells within the specified range and only totals numeric values.

formulas.title: AVERAGE Function Syntax
formulas.worked: =AVERAGE(B2:B21) returns the arithmetic mean of 20 exam scores
formulas.note: AVERAGE automatically divides the SUM of the range by the COUNT of numeric cells in it.

formulas.title: IF Function Syntax
formulas.worked: =IF(A1>=50,"Pass","Fail") displays Pass if A1 is 50 or more, otherwise Fail
formulas.note: The logical test must evaluate to TRUE or FALSE; the two following arguments are what gets returned in each case.

formulas.title: VLOOKUP Function Syntax
formulas.worked: =VLOOKUP(A2,D2:F100,3,FALSE) finds A2's exact match in column D and returns the value in the 3rd column of that range
formulas.note: Setting the fourth argument to FALSE forces an exact match; TRUE or omitting it allows an approximate match.

formulas.title: COUNTIF Function Syntax
formulas.worked: =COUNTIF(C2:C50,"Excel") counts how many cells in C2:C50 contain the text "Excel"
formulas.note: Criteria can be text, numbers, or comparison operators such as ">50" (in quotes).

formulas.title: Absolute Reference Locking
formulas.eq: $Column$Row (dollar signs lock the column and/or row)
formulas.worked: Copying =A1*$B$1 down a column keeps B1 fixed while A1 adjusts to A2, A3, and so on
formulas.note: Press F4 while editing a formula to quickly cycle through relative, absolute, and mixed reference styles.

formulas.title: Percentage Calculation Formula
formulas.eq: = (part ÷ whole) × 100 (or simply format the decimal result as a percentage)
formulas.worked: If A1=45 and B1=180, then =A1/B1 formatted as a percentage displays 25%
formulas.note: Excel's Percentage format automatically multiplies the underlying decimal value by 100 when displaying it.

formulas.title: Total Magnification-style Chaining (Nested Function)
formulas.worked: =ROUND(AVERAGE(A1:A10),2) first averages A1:A10, then rounds that result to 2 decimal places
formulas.note: Excel always calculates the innermost function first, then works outward, similar to standard order of operations.

formulas.title: Slide Timing Total Calculation
formulas.eq: Total show duration = sum of each slide's rehearsed timing
formulas.worked: 10 slides averaging 30 seconds each gives an estimated total show duration of 300 seconds (5 minutes)
formulas.note: Rehearse Timings records each slide's actual duration, which can then be totaled to estimate overall presentation length.

typein.q: What serial number does Excel assign to the date 1/1/1902?
typein.e: Counting days from 1/1/1900 (serial 1), the date 1/1/1902 falls on serial number 732.
^ is the exponentiation operator: 4^3 means 4 raised to the power 3, i.e. 4×4×4 = 64.

typein.q: What does the formula =50% evaluate to?
typein.e: The % operator divides the number by 100, so 50% is stored and used as the decimal value 0.5.
The percent operator divides by 100, so 25% evaluates to the decimal 0.25.
Division and multiplication share the same precedence and are evaluated left to right: 10/5 = 2, then 2×2 = 4.
Parentheses force the addition first: 6+27 = 33, then 33/3 = 11.
Parentheses force the addition first: 2+3 = 5, then 5×4 = 20.
ABS() returns the absolute (unsigned) value of a number, so ABS(-15) = 15.
MOD returns the remainder of a division: 17 divided by 5 is 3 remainder 2, so MOD(17,5) = 2.
FACT() returns the factorial of a number: 5! = 5×4×3×2×1 = 120.

typein.q: Given the values 4, 8, 6, 2, 10 in A1:A5, what does =AVERAGE(A1:A5) return?
Given the values 4, 8, 6, 2, 10 in A1:A5, what does =COUNT(A1:A5) return?
typein.e: COUNT() counts how many cells contain numbers — all 5 cells here contain numeric values.
LEN() counts the number of characters in the text; "Computer" has 8 letters.

typein.q: Given F1 = 38 hours worked, what does =IF(F1>40,(F1-40)*1.5,0) return?
typein.e: Since 38 is not greater than 40, the FALSE branch runs, returning 0 — there is no overtime.
